ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a fixed-bias transistor amplifier circuit, with the power supply labeled +15V; the base bias resistor is labeled 475K, connected from +15V to the base; the collector resistor is labeled 3K, connected from +15V to the collector; the emitter is grounded. Reasoning: Given in the problem β=50, U_BEQ=0.7V. The base current I_B=(15-0.7)/475kΩ=14.3/475000≈30.1μA. The collector current I_C=βI_B=50×30.1μA≈1.505mA. The voltage drop across the collector resistor is I_C R_C≈1.505mA×3kΩ≈4.52V. The emitter is grounded, so U_CEQ=15V-4.52V≈10.48V, taken as approximately 10.5V.
